stemBlocks.value: Think first: Multiplication is buried in the middle of this expression, so clear it before you add or subtract.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p008-q12 from workbook page 8.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply the two fractions, cancelling first.
Set up the subtraction over a common denominator.
Subtract the numerators and convert to a mixed number.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply 12/35 by 7/9 first, cancelling common factors, then add 5/6 and 2/3 and subtract the product using a common denominator.

whyThisWorks.value: The × in the expression is a stronger binding than + or −, so 12/35 × 7/9 is one quantity that must be evaluated before it can be removed from the sum. Cancelling common factors before multiplying keeps the numbers small and avoids simplifying 84/315 afterwards. Addition and subtraction of fractions then only work once every fraction is cut into pieces of the same size, which is what the common denominator 30 provides.

commonErrors.misconception: Working strictly left to right and subtracting 12/35 before multiplying by 7/9.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Working strictly left to right and subtracting 12/35 before multiplying by 7/9.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying 84/315 out and then failing to simplify it to 4/15.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying 84/315 out and then failing to simplify it to 4/15.

commonErrors.misconception: Using 6 × 15 = 90 as the denominator instead of the LCM 30 and then not simplifying.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using 6 × 15 = 90 as the denominator instead of the LCM 30 and then not simplifying.

examTip.value: Cancel across the multiplication sign before you multiply — it turns most CSEC fraction products into single-digit arithmetic.
